light.ao_why: AO baked on the watertight low itself (the proxy's feather flaps are inner shells that black-hole AO rays; spike_beak / vulture lesson); ray length 0.2 u and texels under 0.04 refilled from their neighbours so the basecolor stays near the albedo
light.bake_drop_interior_why: proxy faces with solid on both sides (inner shells under the feather flaps) left out of the bake source so the cage stays tight (spike_beak idiom)
light.uv_island_margin_why: the feather-flap low unwraps into thousands of islands; the default margin starves the atlas (storm_bear / vulture_creature idiom)

rig.spine_why: the body midline is x 0 (slab mid-x z 0.5..4.0: -0.009..+0.005; back-edge centroid -0.03..+0.03); neck root (0, 0.05, 4.15); the head pivot sits between the eyes (eye midpoint x 0.031) and the head bone runs 1.0 u along the FACE direction (perpendicular to the pupil-centre line, yaw 0.36 deg), so the repose heading turns the face straight ahead

chains.name: leg
chains.why: leg slab centroids (yellow texels, stage frame): z 1.38 (+-0.58, 0.62), z 0.98 (+-0.66, 0.57), z 0.59 (+-0.78, 0.42), ankle z 0.42 (+-0.8, 0.38), front toes (y -0.44, z 0.2, x +-0.99); hip inside the body at z 1.9. The pair is mirror-symmetric as generated (centroid differences <= 0.05 u); the +x claws hang 0.070 u above the floor

chains.name: tail
chains.why: the short layered tail on the midline (back edge |x| < 0.3: y 1.84 at z 2.3 -> 2.0 at z 1.1, tip z ~0.7; x -0.04..0.0): centred as generated, a chain so it can sway / be posed

clips.why: PLACEHOLDER (movement + height are the open artist questions): idle = breathe + the kit's tail sway; walk = a stalking bird step (leg swing 8: batch lesson, the kit walk dips the feet below the floor)

targets.why: artist 2026-10-17: a symmetric rest pose. The legs are already near-mirror (joint differences <= 0.05 u) but the +x claws hang 0.070 u above the floor: both legs carried onto their mean, both feet planted on z 0

targets.heading: -y
targets.why: the head straight ahead: the face (perpendicular to the pupil-centre line) points 0.36 deg off -y; the neck takes half, the head the rest; the head is RIGID (below)

rigid.why: the head (mask plate, spike, both eyes, crest feathers) moves as ONE rigid body with the head bone: never deformed or re-sculpted; the eye paint rides on the UVs
the long beak (tip z 3.78) rides rigidly with the head too

Points: stage-1 frame (the feet already on the floor, x0.9849 to the sheet front height 5.90), sheet units; -y = front, +x = the unit's left.
